name: Datsun 210 "Fuji"
hook: Nissan's bosses feared their first race abroad would humiliate them, and instead a one-litre Datsun drove all the way around Australia and won its class.
story:
Picture Australia in August 1958. Sixty-seven cars are lining up to drive right around the continent.

Two of them are small Japanese saloons almost nobody outside Japan has heard of. They are Datsun 210s, with one-litre engines and 34 horsepower. One is red, and named Fuji. The other is white, and named Sakura, for the cherry blossom.

The man behind them is Yutaka Katayama, a Nissan manager. His bosses hated the idea. If the cars broke down abroad, the company would be humiliated. He pushed and argued until he got his cars and his crews.

Then came nineteen days of dust, gravel and long empty roads. More than sixteen thousand kilometres, clockwise around Australia.

Only thirty-six cars reached the finish. Both Datsuns were among them. Fuji won its class, for cars under a thousand cc. Sakura came fourth.

The next spring, Fuji went on show in New York. And Katayama? In 1960 he was sent to America, to help sell Datsuns there.
description: The Datsun 1000, type 210, was Nissan's small family saloon, launched in November 1957. It used Nissan's first one-litre overhead-valve engine, a 988 cc four-cylinder, with leaf springs and drum brakes all round. Two 210s, named Fuji and Sakura, ran the 1958 Mobilgas Trial around Australia. It was Nissan's first international competition. Fuji, car number 19, won Class A and finished 25th overall. The red car survives in Nissan's Heritage Collection.
